title: Would, could: sounding polite
goal: Ask for things politely and naturally
intro: How you ask matters as much as what you ask. “I want water” or “Give me the file” can sound rude in English even when you don’t mean it. Use could, would, may and “would like” to make requests and offers polite. “Kindly” and “do the needful” sound old-fashioned; modern English prefers “Could you please…?”

rules.rule: Could you / Would you + base form …?
examples: Could you send me the link?
Would you mind closing the window?

rules.rule: Can I / Could I / May I …? to ask for something.
examples: Could I have some water, please?
Would you mind waiting a minute?
Would you mind if I sat here?

mistakes.right: Could I have a coffee, please?
mistakes.why: “I want” sounds demanding in a shop.

mistakes.right: Could you please take care of this?

mistakes.why: “Revert back” isn’t used this way outside India. Say “reply” or “get back to me”.

ex.q: ___ you help me with this bag, please?
I’d ___ a table for two, please.
Would you mind ___ the music down?
___ I use your phone for a minute?
Would you mind to send me the file?
ex.fixed: Would you mind sending me the file?
Could I have one masala dosa.

ex.y: Say reply / get back to me.

ex.a: Could you please call me back later?

ex.q: Ask politely for the bill in a restaurant.
a: Could I have the bill please
Could we have the bill please
Can I have the bill please
Can we have the bill please
Could we get the bill please
Could I get the bill please
May I have the bill please
ex.y: Could I have the bill, please?

talk: You are at a hotel. Politely ask for three things (a late checkout, a taxi, extra towels) and offer to help another guest.
